subject: Standby GPU commitment for Heliox APAC pilot
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Erin Walsh <erin@heliox.ai>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@heliox.ai>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Standby GPU commitment for Heliox APAC pilot

Hi Erin / Samir —

Thanks again for the productive product-session yesterday. Per our conversation, Heliox is targeting a mid-May pilot in Singapore with a planned user cohort that should ramp over 4 weeks. You asked about a standby commitment so you don’t hit cold-start latency and so we can reserve capacity ahead of other sales-driven pool allocations.

Quick summary of Heliox ask (as I captured it):
- Pilot start: target week of 2027-05-09
- Expected steady-state: 40 reqs/sec at 512 tokens avg per request at peak; burst tolerance up to 120 reqs/sec for short periods
- Model family: open-llama-v3-like (~13B) with quantized float16 serving preferred; possible H100 preferred for latency targets
- SLA ask: 99.9% availability for reserved pool during pilot window

Internal ask to our ops/sourcing partners (Cc’d): can Redwood provision a standby dedicated pool in APAC for the 4-week pilot window (plus 1-week run-up/fallover)? I sketched two options below — please confirm rough sizing, expected unit cost delta vs hosted, and any lead-time constraints.

Option A (conservative): 6 x H100-equivalent GPUs in a reserved pool + 30% burst buffer (on-demand H100s)
Option B (cost-optimized): 12 x A100-80G (quantized pathways) with tighter batching + 2x H100 warm nodes for spike handling

Attached: heliox_apac_traffic_snapshot.csv (they shared historical traffic for their beta); I also dropped a first-pass standby_capacity_proposal_v1.xlsx with conservative estimator fields.

Goal: align on committed units so Heliox can finalize procurement approvals and Redwood can lock capacity or start procurement. If possible, include our default standby terms (see redwood-standby-terms-draft.pdf) or flag items that Heliox will push back on.

Next steps: Erin, can you confirm whether Ops must guarantee H100s specifically or if A100s with quantization are acceptable for the pilot? Samir, any procurement timeline constraints you want us to know now? Internal: Prio — queue this for capacity planning review before EOD.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Sr. Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@heliox.ai>

Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 12:40:00 +0800
Subject: Re: Standby GPU commitment for Heliox APAC pilot

Thanks, Irene — appreciate the clear options. Quick answers from our side:
- We prefer H100s for the pilot window if you can guarantee latency under 120ms p95 for the 512-token workload. If you can demonstrate comparable latency on A100s with quantized kernels, we could accept that with a 5% price concession.
- Procurement timeline: we need a signed commitment and invoice by 2027-04-20 to satisfy internal CAPEX cycles.
- Contractual ask: 2-week exit window after pilot if results are not satisfactory (Heliox must not be locked into a 12-month term in case product-market-fit diverges).

On traffic: the attached CSV shows internal beta activity for their EU region; the Singapore pilot will likely be slightly higher due to local partners.

Samir
SMS - Lead, Platform Engineering
Heliox AI

Irene — pulled the first-cut numbers from our capacity model and added notes inline. Short version — both options are feasible but trade-offs: latency reliability vs cost.

Assumptions used (from Heliox CSV + conservative ramps):
- Peak inference traffic: 120 reqs/sec bursts (sustained 40 rps)
- Avg 512 tokens / call, with ~1.25 tokens/sec generation time per model step (model-specific)
- Effective batching efficiency: 1.8x on A100 quantized; 2.6x on H100 FP16 kernels

First-cut sizing (service-level pockets):
- Option A: 6 H100s -> p95 latency ~95–130ms depending on batching; supports 120rps with burst buffer at 30% headroom.
- Option B: 12 A100-80G + 2 warm H100s -> p95 ~120–160ms when bursts exceed batching windows; cost ~20–30% lower than all-H100 standby.

Lead times: H100 immediate availability in our Singapore region is limited; reservation lead time ~4–6 weeks to guarantee capacity for May. A100s are available with 2–3 week lead-time.

Procurement note: for a standby reservation we require 50% of the first-month standby fee at signing to lock the pool; full details in the standby_terms.

I’ll update the attached standby_capacity_proposal_v1.xlsx with per-GPU cost slices and a forecast run-rate for the pilot window.

— Priyom
Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference

Thanks — that all helps. A couple clarifying points from procurement/legal: 
1) Heliox will accept A100s only if we can define an objective performance test that we run during a 7-day warmup window. If the p95 target isn't met on A100s, Heliox can convert to H100s at Redwood's published delta pricing.
2) The 2-week exit window Samir mentioned is important; we will sign a 3-month pilot commitment with a 14-day opt-out post-pilot and a separate clause that covers early termination fees pro-rated for committed standby.

Can Redwood provide: a) an A100 vs H100 benchmark doc for the 13B-like model at 512 tokens (p95/p99), and b) a short draft SOW that captures the standby dates, invoicing cadence, and exit terms? We want to hand that to legal by 2027-04-12.

Erin Walsh
Head of Procurement, Heliox AI
